title: Number of Smooth Descent Periods of a Stock
summary: Given an integer array prices representing daily stock prices, count the number of contiguous periods where each day's price is exactly 1 lower than the previous day's price, excluding the first day of the period.
statement: Given an integer array prices representing daily stock prices, count the number of contiguous periods where each day's price is exactly 1 lower than the previous day's price, excluding the first day of the period.
constraints: A period is smooth when each price after the first is exactly one less than its predecessor.
Count all nonempty contiguous smooth periods.
hints: Each day ends one singleton plus every smooth period ending yesterday that can extend.
Maintain the length of the current exactly-one descent run.
If previous-price==1 set run+=1, otherwise run=1; add run to the total.
The run length equals the number of valid starting positions for a period ending today, counting each period at its unique endpoint.
editorial: The run length equals the number of valid starting positions for a period ending today, counting each period at its unique endpoint.

tests.explanation: The four singleton periods plus [3,2], [2,1], and [3,2,1] total seven.
No adjacent pair descends by exactly one, so only four singleton periods count.
